quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you stay out of other vehicles' blind spots. It helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid hazards on the road and gives you an escape route if needed. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is safer than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly alongside another vehicle. This can put you in the vehicle's blind spot. If the driver cannot see you, they may turn into your lane without warning. Riding alongside a vehicle is also dangerous because you cannot escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always the right side of the lane.
Is always the center of the lane.
Is always the left side of the lane.
Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. You should change your lane position based on the road conditions, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then slowly edge forward to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then slowly edge forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign first. Then edge forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Are caused by worn tires.
Happen at night.
Involve riders who are new to their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who are new to their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who have little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes right away.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble because it will make the motorcycle more unstable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean your weight forward and down, and pull off the road safely. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face in a crash.
Only protects you from dirt.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be worn with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You use your left foot to operate it.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you sleepy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nervousness can make you sleepy and reduce your ability to ride safely. Before riding, know how your medication will affect you.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear produces an effect similar to:

options.text: Speeding up.
Braking.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you downshift to a lower gear, it slows down your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark. Slow down and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane unsafely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
The rider may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing only in areas where passing is legal and safe. Always follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do to maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from leaning.
Look through the turn to plan ahead.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan ahead.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head to maintain direction control. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage lane sharing by other drivers?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center portion of the lane
By riding in the left portion of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to reduce open space on both sides of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to share your lane.

questions.question: If a wind blast from a passing vehicle hits you, you will have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legal intoxication. It is illegal and unsafe to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should not:

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be scratch-free, protect against impacts, allow side visibility, fit securely, and allow air to flow. An airtight shield traps moisture, causing fogging that blocks your vision.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
Riding conditions are normal.
The roadway is wet.
You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs longer to stop, such as on wet roads. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that lets oncoming drivers see you first. For example, if turning right at a blind corner, stay toward the left side of your lane rather than the center.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, gradually reduce speed by closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Cannot tip over.
Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Can handle corners at any speed.
Should not carry any items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: After you start the motorcycle
Before you start the motorcycle
While riding
At a red light

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.
